goal: Reconstruct the evidentiary chain from reported Jiuzhang/DeepSeek technical developments to claims about present cryptographic compromise, preserving observation, inference, hypothesis, prediction, and engineering consequence as distinct governed states.
promotion_boundary: Do not promote Gaussian-boson-sampling advantage, general Chinese quantum capability, classified-capability speculation, harvest-now/decrypt-later risk, or stronger rhetorical framing into a finding that RSA-2048/ECC is presently broken or that Western encrypted traffic is currently being quantum-decrypted without direct authoritative evidence.

source_trigger.title: They’re Coming? They’re Already Here — 4 Trillion Times Faster
source_trigger.author: Zoli Bill Apró

tasks.release_condition: Jiuzhang performance claims are reconstructed with the workload boundary preserved and no conversion into arbitrary-compute or cryptanalytic performance.
tasks.progress_note: Nature primary publication reconstructed. Jiuzhang 4.0 is bounded to Gaussian boson sampling; 1,024 squeezed states, 8,176 modes, and detection events up to 3,050 photons are captured. No Shor/RSA/ECC result is present in the captured source.

tasks.object: Evidence for cryptographically relevant quantum attack capability
tasks.release_condition: Any claim of current RSA-2048/ECC compromise is traceable to direct technical evidence rather than extrapolation from unrelated quantum advantage experiments.
tasks.progress_note: Peer-reviewed 2021 RSA-2048 resource estimate and 2025 updated preprint estimate captured. Both require Shor-family error-corrected architectures under explicit assumptions. Jiuzhang optical modes/squeezed states are not interchangeable with physical/logical qubits, and no architecture mapping or operational RSA-2048/ECC break is established.

tasks.object: NIST post-quantum cryptography standards and migration guidance
tasks.release_condition: Claims about whether quantum-resistant encryption is available are tested against authoritative current standards.
tasks.progress_note: NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM, FIPS 204 ML-DSA, and FIPS 205 SLH-DSA are established as finalized August 2024 standards ready for implementation. NIST recommends migration now and maintains transition guidance toward removal of quantum-vulnerable algorithms by 2035, earlier for high-risk systems.

tasks.release_condition: DeepSeek references are separated from unrelated quantum-computing capability claims and admitted only within their supported scope.
tasks.progress_note: Official 2026-04-24 DeepSeek V4 Preview release reconstructed: 1M context, V4-Pro 1.6T/49B active parameters, V4-Flash 284B/13B active parameters. No quantum-computing or RSA/ECC cryptanalytic bridge is established by the release.

tasks.object: LinkedIn article numerical and causal claim ledger
tasks.release_condition: Every material numerical/security claim is classified as observed fact, sourced statement, inference, hypothesis, prediction, unsupported extrapolation, or engineering consequence.
tasks.progress_note: User-provided profile Activity screenshot now preserves a stronger visible title: 'They're Not Coming. They're Already Here. And They're 4 Trillion Times Faster', with visible associations to #Cybercrime, #PostQuantumCryptography, and #IdentityHarvest. This establishes a rhetorical state transition from uncertainty-framed to categorical present-tense assertion. It does not establish the underlying operational cryptanalytic claim. Full article/post text remains required for complete numerical and causal claim decomposition.

tasks.object: Claims of classified Chinese operational quantum cryptanalytic capability
tasks.release_condition: Classified-capability speculation is either supported by independently reproducible authoritative evidence or retained explicitly as unresolved hypothesis.
tasks.progress_note: No authoritative public evidence has been admitted that establishes a classified Chinese system presently breaking RSA-2048/ECC. NIST's current public posture remains that cryptographically relevant quantum computers do not yet exist.

tasks.release_condition: ERL findings are translated into bounded architectural requirements without treating the source article’s strongest security claims as established fact.
tasks.progress_note: Twelve candidate controls derived covering algorithm admissibility, crypto agility, dual-stack coexistence, downgrade resistance, retirement, HNDL exposure classification, evidence-bound triggers, provenance/reconstruction, credential-authority preservation, provider/runtime independence, fail-safe transition, and independent compromise-state representation. Cross-repository installation is intentionally not performed until the target repository handoff is read.

blocked_next_actions: QAC-005 full claim decomposition requires reproducible complete LinkedIn article/post text or equivalent source custody; the rhetorical transition itself is now preserved.
QAC-006 requires new authoritative public evidence before any stronger operational-capability classification is admissible.
Cross-repository installation of QAC-007 requirements requires selection of the target owner repository and reading its current *_MIRROR_HANDOFF.md before mutation.
duplicate_execution_rule: Before acquiring or creating a record, search the ERL source-posture, evidence, intake, and rhetoric surfaces for an existing Jiuzhang, DeepSeek, post-quantum, RSA/ECC, harvest-now/decrypt-later, or Apró LinkedIn activity object. Reuse preserved custody where available.
completion_condition: The article’s technical and security propositions are independently reconstructable with explicit evidence-state transitions, and no operational cryptographic-compromise finding exceeds the strongest authoritative evidence.
